It's come to my understanding that not everyone knows that I have an alternate oversized card for Mr. Fixer (Stance Shifting Master) on my site.  It was (and still is) part of the general oversized hero hp tracker .zip file, but I've pulled it out into its own entry on the printable accessories page now to increase its discoverability.

I play with it every time I play Fixer, and it really makes him more fun to play.  It encourages you to play new styles and tools to get a bonus to damage.  The constant shift between styles and tools throughout the game feels like exactly the kind of thing a Zen martial arts mechanic master would do to keep his enemies off balance.

posts.cooked:
Last night, we played a game of SotM with a truly epic table bump, sending the dice we were using to track hp of each of Citizen Dawn's minions flying.  This morning, I vowed to start using the tiny hp trackers I have on my site instead of dice, but I still don't love them enough to use them.  They're too complicated.

So I iterated again and came up with a third version of them that I think gets it right.  They're easy to assemble, simple to use, and while you do still need to use both hands to hold it while adjusting the spinner, I think the advantages are strong enough that I'm finally going to start using them instead of dice to track minion hp.

The new file is on my site if you're interested in checking it out.

posts.name: Spiff
posts.cooked:
Updates to my site tonight:

  • I've rolled the Shattered Timelines accessories in with all the others accessories, so now you'll get them along with each type of accessory rather than in a .zip of just ST stuff.
  • I've taken all non-standard oversized character cards out of the regular .zip files and now have a "custom characters" section in which you can find anything I've made changes to which make them different from the approved versions.  Currently in that section are:

 

  • Akash'bhuta: Nature's Fury. Akash'bhuta starts with a few Primeval Limbs in play at the start of the game, which makes the game a bit more action-packed from the get-go.
  • Ambuscade: Trapmaster. Changes the way trap cards work (they trigger immediately when revealed rather than being buried back in the deck) and puts traps into play face-down at the start of the game, waiting to be revealed when Devices are destroyed. Changes Ambuscade from a faceroll to a fun challenge.
  • Gloomweaver: Extra Gloom. Increases the challenge of Gloomweaver quite a bit by making zombies much tougher and making it so that heroes who are pinned can't deal damage to anything but their pin until it's been destroyed. This version feels more like a "3" difficulty villain than his normal version does.
  • Mr. Fixer: Stance-Shifting Master. Changes Fixer's base power so that if a stance or tool was played that turn, his Strike ability does one extra damage. This encourages the player to continually swap out stances and tools like a good martial arts mechanic would, but doesn't penalize you if you want to keep the stance/tool you have in play.
  • Wraith: Rook City Detective. This changes Rook City Wraith's base power by just a bit, allowing Wraith to not only discard or play a revealed environment card, put also put it back on top of the deck if you want. This increases the amount of deck control the power provides to make it feel more right to me.

The ONLY complaint I have about this game is that table real estate by the end of games gets a little chaotic.   I love the oversized villain cards, but it exacerbates the problem.  

 

Does anyone know  something that can be used for card stands?  I'm thinking something along the lines of Scrabble tile holders.  Something we can stick on the far edge of the table and prop the card upright in.  I don't actually own a copy of Scrabble, so I can't test out those specifically, but I'm guessing they won't work because I don't think they have a proper groove and probably not enough weight.  

 

There are probably some desk accessories at Office Depot or Staples that are bottom-heavy enough and have something to hold notes or paper. Or maybe even countertop business card or flyer holders.  A bit more pricey and bulky than I'd like, but I think anyone in this thread is all about going the deluxe route for presenting and playing this game!

 

I just had another idea.  I'm going to try to convert a couple of cardboard trading card boxes (the ones that hold a thousand cards) into something that looks exactly like a mini comic book longbox.

I've been playing around with the office supplies I have lying around, and binder clips seem to work pretty well in a ghetto pinch.  Two ways.  One is to clamp the clip on the extreme edge of the bottom of the card and fold out the 'handles' to act as a kind of base.  I'm using the super-mini binder clips and they aren't leaving any indentations on the sides of the cards, but I also have them in sleeves so indentations should never be a problem.  An alternate way is to just place the card in between the clip and the folded back handle (I'll post pics later).  It's a bit more of an extreme angle, but still takes up a lot less room than laying them flat.
